facts.text: Paw Paw’s name comes from the Wyoming Valley in Pennsylvania, where many early settlers originated.
By 1878, the village finally got a railroad connection, was home to two newspapers, three churches and was christened, officially, as Paw Paw.
In between, you might enjoy viewing some of Paw Paw’s downtown historic commercial and residential landmarks with a self‑guided walking tour sponsored by the Village’s Historical Commission.
The first stagecoach station, known as a 'Tavern,' was built along Chicago Road and operated by Isaac Balding.
A 2005 federal grant helped Paw Paw construct a water tower, now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Paw Paw was officially established in 1882 and celebrated its 125th anniversary in 2007.
